text:
ryan: Internal announcement: rolling out "minute pacing with soft rollover" for hosted API customers starting 2026-09-01 00:00 UTC. This is a change to how transient spikes are handled and how unused free credits can be carried forward during the pilot.

nina: TL;DR: we will meter pacing at 60s granularity for smoothing decisions and allow up to $250/month of unused free credits to roll into a small rollover pool per account during the pilot. Unit prices unchanged.

ryan: Key customer impact: fewer noisy overage events; small rollover balance shows as invoice line "rollover_credit_applied". Retro adjustments window: 30 days.

dev-bot: New CSV columns for invoice export v4: account_id,period_start,period_end,total_tokens,billed_tokens,minute_peak,rollover_credit_applied,rollover_amount. API flag: ?include_rollover=true.

nina: Support ops, please prep two short canned replies: one for startups and one for enterprise customers. Example Q/A: "Will this change my contract?" -> "No, reserved/dedicated contracts are unaffected unless you opt in."

accounts: Finance note - rollover credits are non-refundable, capped at $250 per account during pilot, visible on console and invoices. Cap for auto retro credits: $2,000/account lifetime during pilot.

ryan: Engineering note - there will be a new header X-Redwood-Pacing: minute accepted from launch. Old behavior remains supported for 60 days. We'll publish a migration guide.

ops-bot: Created ticket RW-ROLL-2026 and scheduled tasks for the August checklist. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-ROLL-2026 :white_check_mark:

nina: Action items:
- @nina: publish pilot FAQ + sample invoice.
- @ryan: coordinate customer email for high-impact accounts.
- @dev-bot: PR for meterer changes and CSV schema.
- @accounts: finalize invoice label and PDF placement.
- @ops-bot: weekly pilot metrics report.

ryan: We'll run an internal support dry-run next Tuesday. Ping here for review or if you need to opt any customer out. Thanks! :thumbsup:
